newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Still setting up.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Still setting up.

text.p: Asian debt markets were quiet on Tuesday as bankers continued to line up the first deals of the new year.
Bankers said Korean banks continue to take bids for what could become this year's benchmark deal. Shinhan Bank and Cho Hung Bank are in the running for the first transaction.
"The banks are still trying to get a few basis points out of the OECD membership," said one syndicate manager.
South Korea was invited to join the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development late last year.
Price talk for the bank issues is in the high teens, with A2-rated Shinhan trying for a few basis points less its than A3-rated counterparts, the syndicate manager said.
Cho Hung Bank's last transaction, a US$200 million three-year floating rate note launched in November, paid about 23 basis points all-in.

U.S. mortgage agencies Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac launched global bonds today. In Asia, central banks and some institutional investors, particularly in Japan, are the usual buyers of such high-grade agency paper.
In the loan markets, 17 banks signed a HK$6.3255 billion five-year term loan facility to finance a property development project in Hong Kong.
The project, Belcher Gardens, on Hong Kong island's Pokfulam Road is undertaken by developer Ranex Investments Ltd, which is held by a consortium of Hong Kong property developers.
Ranex is 51 percent held by Shun Tak Holdings and 29 percent by Sun Hung Kai Properties. New World Development Co Ltd and Liu Chong Hing Investment each hold 10 percent.
The loan is guaranteed up to 48.33 percent by Sun Hung Kai, 31.67 percent by Shun Tak while New World and Liu Chong Hing are responsible for 10.00 percent each.
It pays a margin of 100 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate for years one to four and 130 basis points over HIBOR thereafter until maturity.
With fees, the all-in return is 125 basis points over HIBOR.
Arrangers are HSBC Investment Bank Asia, Hang Seng Finance, Westdeutsche Landesbank, Chase Manhattan Asia and China Development Finance Co (HK).

In other news, analysts and traders in Thailand welcomed a plan for the first government bond in several years, saying it would create a needed benchmark for the secondary market and cheaper funds for state enterprises.
"It is a very good move. We would really like to see it happen soon," Somjin Sornpaisarn, deputy general manager of the Bond Dealers' Club, told Reuters in Bangkok.
Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said Monday that the government plans to issue government bonds for the first time in 10 years this year.
